summary_paragraph: A man with a history of type 2 diabetes, kidney transplant, peripheral vascular disease, and prior amputations was admitted for osteomyelitis in the right index finger and right foot, presenting with pain, foul drainage, and fever. Imaging and biopsy confirmed bone infection in both sites. He underwent amputation of the right index finger tip and a transmetatarsal amputation of the right foot. Cultures grew Proteus mirabilis, sensitive to ertapenem. Due to equivocal margins in the foot, he was discharged on a prolonged course of outpatient IV ertapenem via a PICC line. His hypertension was managed with adjustment of labetalol to 600 mg twice daily, and his transplant function remained stable with continued immunosuppression. He was discharged home ambulatory with walker assistance, with plans for weekly lab monitoring and follow-up with podiatry and infectious disease.
problems: Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
